sentences.text: Researchers conducted a randomized, sham-controlled crossover study with ten healthy human participants who performed a P300 speller task before and after stimulation while an attention-demanding task was active. The team measured P300 peak amplitudes, the ability to distinguish targets from non-targets, and offline classification accuracy across different brain channels.

Real stimulation led to a statistically significant improvement in offline discrimination accuracy specifically at the P4 brain channel compared to sham stimulation, yet it did not result in improved real-time character selection performance. Participants with lower initial performance showed larger improvements, though these gains were not statistically significant, suggesting tDCS might help this specific group more.
The authors conclude that while the method is feasible for modulating brain activity, more research is needed to understand how these local changes affect the full decoding process.
